prompt: The Vite planner's preview server is asked for `/courses/spanish` by `curl`. What comes back?
hint: Lesson 17 showed the same answer for every address.

choices.text: The Spanish course's sessions, drawn as a list
choices.why: That is what the browser shows after the script has run and fetched the data; `curl` runs no script.

choices.text: A redirect to `/`, where the router takes over
choices.why: The preview server answers the address with a page, not a redirect; the router reads the address once it runs.

choices.text: An empty `<div id="app">` and a script
choices.why: Right. The HTML is the same shell for every address, and everything visible is drawn by the script.

choices.text: The course's title and description, with the sessions left for the script
choices.why: That would be a page drawn partly on the server; the Vite build sends no words of the page at all.

prompt: Which of these are costs of client-side rendering that the lesson names? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three costs, and readers who turn JavaScript off are not one of them.

choices.text: A blank screen until the script and the data have arrived
choices.why: Right. On a cheap phone on a slow network that is seconds of white.

choices.text: Many readers browse with JavaScript turned off
choices.why: The lesson says few people do, and that this is not the cost.

choices.text: A link preview finds an empty `<div>`
choices.why: Right. The program that builds the preview reads the HTML without running it.

choices.text: An error at start-up leaves nothing drawn
choices.why: Right. If the script fails, the blank page is all the reader gets.

choices.text: Each tick needs a full page reload from the server
choices.why: A tick in the Vite planner sends a request and redraws in place; nothing reloads.

prompt: In a Nuxt page, what is hydration?
hint: It happens in the browser, after the HTML is already on the screen.

choices.text: The server turning the components' output into HTML
choices.why: That is the server-side render, the first half; hydration is the second.

choices.text: The browser's Vue attaching itself to the elements the server sent
choices.why: Right. It runs the same components and attaches them instead of drawing new elements.

choices.text: The browser fetching `/api/courses` after the page is shown
choices.why: The data came inside the page, in the payload; the built page made no such request.

choices.text: Drawing the page again in the browser and swapping it for the server's
choices.why: Vue does not draw the page again; it walks the server's elements and attaches to them.

prompt: With JavaScript off, a reader ticks the 21st on the Nuxt week page and loads `/` again. The footer still says 75 of 195. Why?
hint: The box did tick. What sends the `PATCH`?

choices.text: The `@change` that sends the `PATCH` is attached by hydration
choices.why: Right. Without JavaScript the checkbox ticks itself and nothing tells the server.

choices.text: The server rejected the tick because the page had not hydrated
choices.why: The server never heard of the tick; no request was sent at all.

choices.text: The page was served from a cached copy
choices.why: The dev server keeps no copy here; the reload drew the server's data, which had not changed.

choices.text: A checkbox cannot be ticked before Vue is running
choices.why: It can and was: a checkbox ticks itself. What is missing is the listener.

prompt: From the built Nuxt server, how many requests did the week page make in the browser?
hint: Count the `net` lines after `node .output/server/index.mjs`.

prompt: None of the built week page's requests is `/api/courses`, yet the page shows the sessions and hydrates. Where did the browser get the data?
hint: Lesson 20 is about it.

choices.text: From `localStorage`, saved on an earlier visit
choices.why: The planner keeps nothing in the browser; the data comes from the server.

choices.text: From a `/_nuxt/` chunk, where the build compiled the sessions
choices.why: The chunks are code and stylesheets; the sessions change and are not compiled in.

choices.text: From reading the rows back out of the HTML it was sent
choices.why: Vue does not parse data out of markup; it hydrates with the data the server passed along.

choices.text: From the payload sent with the HTML
choices.why: Right. The server sent what `useFetch` received along with the page.

prompt: The built server printed `Listening on http://___:3000`, the address meaning every network the computer is on.
hint: Not `localhost`.

prompt: It is 23:30 in São Paulo on the 21st, the built Nuxt server runs in UTC, and the week page computes `today` on both sides. What does the reader see?
hint: Production repairs a missing element and leaves an attribute alone.

choices.text: The 22nd highlighted, and `(today)` on the 21st
choices.why: Right. Two todays: the server's highlight stayed and the browser's `(today)` was added.

choices.text: The 22nd highlighted and labelled `(today)`, as the server drew it
choices.why: The `(today)` is an element the browser expected on the 21st, and production makes a missing element.

choices.text: The 21st highlighted and labelled `(today)`, as the browser corrects it
choices.why: That is what the dev server ends with; the built one does not fix the class.

choices.text: An error page, because hydration completed with mismatches
choices.why: Production logs one line and carries on; the page works and is quietly wrong.

prompt: Why does the line `const today = isoDate(new Date())` produce a mismatch only some of the time?
hint: The two dates agree for 21 hours of the day.

choices.text: `new Date()` returns a different value on each call
choices.why: It does, by milliseconds; `isoDate` keeps only the day, and the day is what differs.

choices.text: Server and browser read their own clocks in their own time zones
choices.why: Right. In the last three hours of São Paulo's day, UTC is already on the next date.

choices.text: The server caches the page, so its date is from an earlier request
choices.why: Nothing caches the week page; the server draws it per request with its own clock.

choices.text: Hydration runs `isoDate` only when the data has changed
choices.why: Hydration runs the components every time; what differs is the clock each side reads.

prompt: Which of these, read by a component during render, are mismatches waiting to happen? Choose all that apply.
hint: Anything that is not the same on the server and in the browser.

choices.text: `Math.random()`
choices.why: Right. Each side draws its own number.

choices.text: The sessions `useFetch` returned
choices.why: The server decides those and the browser receives them in the payload, so both draw the same.

choices.text: A value read from `localStorage`
choices.why: Right. The server has no `localStorage` at all.

choices.text: An id made by `useId()`
choices.why: That is the fix for counter ids: `useId()` gives the same id on both sides.

choices.text: The window's width
choices.why: Right. There is no window on the server.

prompt: How many routes did `nuxt generate` prerender for the planner?
hint: The line that starts `ℹ Prerendered`.

prompt: How did `nuxt generate` know to render the three course pages?
hint: A page no link reaches is not generated unless it is listed.

choices.text: It rendered every file in `app/pages`, with each id from `courses.json`
choices.why: A dynamic page has no list of ids; generation does not read the data file to invent addresses.

choices.text: It followed the `<NuxtLink>`s on `/`
choices.why: Right. It rendered `/`, read its links and rendered what they lead to.

choices.text: The route rules listed them
choices.why: No rule names the course pages for prerendering; in the route rules section they get `swr`.

choices.text: It asked the router for every route with a parameter
choices.why: The router knows the pattern `/courses/:id`, not which ids exist.

prompt: The generated planner is put on a host that only sends files, and a reader ticks a session. What happens to the tick?
hint: Where does the API exist?

choices.text: It is written into `_payload.json`, and the next visitor sees it
choices.why: A static host writes nothing; the files are as the build left them.

choices.text: It is kept until the next `nuxt generate`, which renders it in
choices.why: Nothing keeps it: the data of the files is the data of the build, read from `courses.json`.

choices.text: The page sends it to `/api/sessions/…`, and the host forwards it to Nitro
choices.why: There is no Nitro behind a host that only sends files.

choices.text: The `PATCH` has no server to answer it
choices.why: Right. A generated planner could show a week; it could not keep one.

prompt: With `'/courses/**': { swr: 60 }`, a session is ticked, and a minute later `/courses/spanish` is requested twice. What do the two requests get?
hint: The first one sets off the new render and does not wait for it.

choices.text: The first the old copy, the second the new one
choices.why: Right. The transcript counted 1 and then 2.

choices.text: Both the new page, because the minute is up
choices.why: After the window the first request is still answered from the copy, at once.

choices.text: Both the old copy, until another sixty seconds pass
choices.why: The first request after the window starts a render in the background, and the second gets it.

choices.text: The first waits for a fresh render, the second gets it from the copy
choices.why: That is ordinary caching; `swr` answers at once from the copy and renders behind it.

prompt: In `routeRules`, `'/about': { ___: true }` draws the page once, by the build, into `.output/public`.
hint: The word `nuxt generate`'s output used for every route.

prompt: A team protects `/admin` with a route rule that redirects anyone who is not signed in. What does the lesson's advisory teach about that?
hint: GHSA-vjh5-4x84-xrqp, and the general lesson after it.

choices.text: It is safe once Nuxt is at 4.6.2, which fixed the capitals
choices.why: 4.6.2 fixed that one bypass; the lesson's point is that a pattern on an address is the wrong place for a lock.

choices.text: It is safe if the rule uses `headers` rather than `redirect`
choices.why: The advisory covered both kinds, `headers` and `redirect` alike.

choices.text: The check must also be enforced by the code that serves the page, or by the host
choices.why: Right. A rule decides rendering and caching; it is not a lock.

choices.text: It is safe if `/admin` is prerendered, so no server answers it
choices.why: A prerendered page is a file anyone can download; prerendering removes the server that would check.

prompt: How does Nuxt's `isr` relate to the `swr` of the planner's course pages?
hint: Same idea, different keeper.

choices.text: The same keeping, done by the hosts that support it, in their own network
choices.why: Right. The copy lives in the host's network rather than in the server.

choices.text: `isr` renders every page at build time, `swr` none
choices.why: That is closer to `prerender`; `isr` also renders on demand and keeps the copy.

choices.text: `isr` sends `cache-control: no-store`, so nothing is kept
choices.why: `no-store` is what the planner's `/api/**` rule sends; `isr` exists to keep a copy.

choices.text: `isr` is `ssr: false` with a cache: the page is drawn in the browser
choices.why: `ssr: false` sends an empty shell; an `isr` page arrives drawn.

prompt: The fix makes `today` a `ref('')` that `onMounted` sets. Why does that end the mismatch?
hint: What is `today` during the server's render, and during the browser's first one?

choices.text: `onMounted` runs before hydration, so the browser draws the right day from the start
choices.why: It runs after hydration, and only in the browser; that is why the first drawings agree.

choices.text: `onMounted` sends the browser's date to the server, which draws it
choices.why: Nothing is sent; the server keeps drawing with `today` empty.

choices.text: A ref is excluded from hydration checks
choices.why: Vue compares what a ref draws like anything else; here the ref is simply the same on both sides.

choices.text: Both first drawings have `today` empty and match no row, so they agree
choices.why: Right. Then `onMounted` sets it and the one row is redrawn, as any ref change would.

prompt: What does the server send for the footer's `<ClientOnly>` time zone line?
hint: `curl` shows the server's HTML.

choices.text: `Days are counted in UTC`, the server's own zone
choices.why: That is what drawing the line on the server would have said, and the reason it is client-only.

choices.text: Nothing, and the footer has an empty gap until hydration
choices.why: That is what happens with no `#fallback`; the planner gives one.

choices.text: `Days are counted in America/Sao_Paulo`, read from the request
choices.why: The server is not told the reader's zone; only the browser reports it.

choices.text: The `#fallback`: `Days are counted in your browser's time zone`
choices.why: Right. A sentence true for every reader, and no mention of UTC.

prompt: A team adds `Weather.client.vue` to `app/components` and uses it on the week page. What does the server do with it?
hint: The name says something, as `Clock.client.vue`'s does.

choices.text: Renders it, and the browser renders it again after hydration
choices.why: Rendering it on both sides is what the `.client` suffix exists to prevent.

choices.text: Leaves it out, as if each use were wrapped in `<ClientOnly>`
choices.why: Right. The suffix makes the component browser-only wherever it is used.

choices.text: Refuses to build until the page wraps it in `<ClientOnly>`
choices.why: The suffix replaces the wrapper; nothing has to be added.

choices.text: Renders it once at build time, like a prerendered page
choices.why: That is `prerender`, a route rule about a page, not a component's name.

prompt: Which modes are open to the lesson's hydration mismatches?
hint: Which modes send HTML that is already drawn?

choices.text: Only SSR, because only there a server renders per request
choices.why: SSG and `swr` send drawn HTML too, and a generated page with a build-time `today` is a mismatch with no server at all.

choices.text: Every mode except CSR, SSG included
choices.why: Right. Each of them hydrates, so what only the browser knows has to wait for hydration.

choices.text: SSR and `swr`, but not SSG, which needs no server
choices.why: Needing no server does not stop a page hydrating; the generated `index.html` showed it.

choices.text: Every mode, CSR included
choices.why: CSR draws only in the browser; with one drawing there is nothing to disagree with.

prompt: Why does the lesson take `swr` off the course pages before the planner is deployed?
hint: Who reads a course page, and who changes it?

choices.text: A page with `swr` cannot be read by a search engine
choices.why: It arrives drawn, which a search engine reads well; that is why a catalogue uses it.

choices.text: Sixty seconds of rendering is too slow
choices.why: The sixty seconds are how long the copy is kept, not how long a render takes.

choices.text: Its reader edits it, and a reload would show the old copy
choices.why: Right. `swr` suits pages many read and few change; a ticked session vanishing on reload is the opposite.

choices.text: `swr` breaks the `PATCH` to `/api/sessions/…`
choices.why: The `PATCH` worked; the API has its own `no-store` rule. Only the HTML was stale.

prompt: Match each part of the planner to the way the lesson's last section renders it.
hint: The list under "The planner's choices".

pairs.left: The reader's day on the week

right_distractors: from a copy at most a minute old

prompt: Put these moments of one visit to the Nuxt week page in order.
hint: The page is readable before it answers a click.
items: The server runs the page's components
The HTML arrives with the payload
The browser downloads the same components

prompt: A shop's product page is the same for everybody, is read thousands of times a day, changes twice a day, and greets a signed-in reader by name. Following the lesson, how is it rendered?
hint: Two questions: is it the same for every reader, and how soon must a change reach it?

choices.text: SSR per request, so the name is in the HTML
choices.why: The name is one reader's, and putting it in the server's HTML gives up the copy thousands of readers share.

choices.text: Prerendered at build time, name included
choices.why: A build has no reader to greet, and twice a day would mean deploying twice a day.

choices.text: Kept with `swr`, the greeting drawn in the browser
choices.why: Right. Shared and rarely changed suits a kept copy; the part that belongs to one reader waits for the browser.

choices.text: `ssr: false`, since one part depends on who is reading
choices.why: That sends an empty shell to every reader and every search engine for the sake of one line.
